title: Lists and Recursion in Prolog
description: Two list relations: my_last finds the last element by recursion on the tail, and rev reverses a list with an accumulator.

steps.description: These two clauses define `my_last`. The page says lists are written `[1,2,3]`, with the head/tail pattern `[H|T]`, and that recursion is the norm. The first clause says `X` is the last element of a one-element list `[X]`. The second says `X` is the last element of `[_|T]` when `X` is the last element of the tail `T`. The underscore is a variable whose name you do not use.
`rev(List, Rev) :- rev_acc(List, [], Rev).` starts the reversal with an empty accumulator. The page notes there is no return: `rev/2` relates a list to its reversal.

`rev_acc` is the accumulator helper. `rev_acc([], Acc, Acc)` is the base case: when the input list is empty, the accumulator is the result. `rev_acc([H|T], Acc, Rev)` moves the head `H` onto the front of the accumulator and recurses on the tail `T`.

steps.question: The page says the query `?- rev([1,2,3], R).` gives which result?
